explanations.pilot_light: Slight increase to replicate static assets in S3 to DR region, but data requests served by CloudFront will not change.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light - CloudFront serves from edge, no DR region cost.
explanations.backup_restore: Nothing provisioned in DR region.
explanations.active_active: Slight increase to replicate static assets; data volumes served by CloudFront unchanged.

explanations.pilot_light: Logs volume unchanged. Metrics cost increases as they exist in DR region (mostly reporting zero). Alerts duplicated in DR.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light with slightly more metrics from warm standby compute.
explanations.backup_restore: Minimal increase for metrics on data/snapshots moved into new region.
explanations.active_active: Logs unchanged. Metrics double across regions. Alerts duplicated.

explanations.backup_restore: CloudWatch Events (EventBridge) bills per event published; rules and bus definitions are free. Nothing runs in DR, so nothing publishes.
explanations.pilot_light: Event buses and rules deployed in DR cost nothing until events flow, and no events flow until failover.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light: per-event billing means the idle DR bus is free even with warm compute running, unless DR-side workloads publish events.
explanations.active_active: Event volume splits across regions; total events published are unchanged, so no additional charge.

explanations.pilot_light: No provisioned DMS instances in secondary region. DMS remains inactive until failover.
explanations.warm_standby: DMS instances running at reduced capacity (~10%). Inactive until secondary becomes primary.
explanations.backup_restore: No provisioned DMS instances in secondary region.
explanations.active_active: Assuming 50-50 workload split. DMS instance sizes could be reduced in both regions.

explanations.backup_restore: PITR plus AWS Backup cross-region copy. No Global Table; storage-only cost is small fraction of baseline.
explanations.pilot_light: Global Tables replica in DR region. Replicates writes (rWRU at ~$1.25/M) and storage; no read traffic in DR. Multiplier captures binary cost shape.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light. Global Tables has no scaled-down replica option; either you have a replica or you don't.
explanations.active_active: Same as pilot light, plus DR region serves traffic. Read costs split 50/50 across regions; write costs unchanged.

explanations.pilot_light: Pay for running load balancers in secondary region. No consumption-based costs since not serving workloads. ~20% for ELB hours.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light - ELBs running but minimal traffic.
explanations.backup_restore: Nothing provisioned in DR region.
explanations.active_active: Second load balancer runs in the DR Region (added hours); traffic splits across Regions so total capacity-unit (LCU) charges don't increase.

explanations.pilot_light: Pay for running load balancers in secondary region. No consumption-based costs since not serving workloads. ~20% for ELB hours.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light - ELBs running but minimal traffic.

explanations.active_active: Second load balancer runs in the DR Region (added hours); traffic splits across Regions so total capacity-unit (LCU) charges don't increase.

explanations.pilot_light: No provisioned compute capacity in secondary region.
explanations.warm_standby: Scaled-down but fully functional fleet at ~50% of primary; Auto Scaling ramps to 100% on failover.
explanations.backup_restore: Nothing provisioned in DR region.
explanations.active_active: Full capacity in each Region so either absorbs the other's load with no ramp; total compute roughly doubles the single-Region baseline.

explanations.warm_standby: EBS scales with the DR EC2 footprint, ~50% at warm standby.
explanations.backup_restore: Stateless EC2 tier recovers from AMIs and IaC; no EBS snapshots copied to DR. AMI storage is per-image and negligible.
explanations.active_active: EBS mirrors full compute in both Regions; volumes duplicated at 100%.

explanations.active_active: Full-capacity ECS tasks in each Region so either absorbs the other's load with no ramp; total task compute roughly doubles.

explanations.backup_restore: No DR-region cluster, so no control plane fee until failover bring-up. Container images replicate under ECR, not this line.
explanations.pilot_light: The EKS control plane bills a flat hourly fee per cluster whether or not workloads run, so a pilot-light cluster doubles this line even at zero nodes. EC2 worker nodes bill under EC2, not here.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light: the control plane fee is flat, so the DR cluster doubles this line regardless of warm node count. Warm EC2 node capacity bills under EC2. EKS Fargate pods, if used, add to this line only while running.
explanations.active_active: A full control plane runs in each region, doubling this line. Worker capacity in both regions bills under EC2 (EKS Fargate pod usage would land on this line).

explanations.backup_restore: AWS Backup cross-region copy at warm-tier pricing; ~20% of source storage cost.

explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light. EFS Replication is the same primitive across postures.
explanations.active_active: EFS does not support multi-region active/active. Treat as warm standby with DR-region mount targets active.

explanations.backup_restore: AWS Backup cross-region copy of the file system. Backup vault storage plus incremental transfer; 0.5 is conservative and assumes multi-snapshot retention in the DR region. No DR-region file system runs.
explanations.pilot_light: A standing DR file system at full provisioned storage and throughput capacity (FSx bills provisioned capacity whether used or not), kept in sync via SnapMirror (FSx for ONTAP) or scheduled AWS Backup copies (other FSx types).
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light: the standing DR file system bills its full provisioned capacity across postures.
explanations.active_active: FSx has no native multi-region active/active. Treat as warm standby with the DR file system live and mounted.

explanations.backup_restore: Cache data is ephemeral; no backup needed. The cache rebuilds from the source database on failover.
explanations.pilot_light: Global Datastore secondary cluster at ~30% of primary node count.
explanations.warm_standby: Global Datastore secondary at ~65% of primary; ready to absorb traffic on failover.
explanations.active_active: Same as warm standby. Global Datastore is single-leader; true active/active requires app-level dual-write.

explanations.warm_standby: Scaled-down EMR cluster at ~50% of primary; Auto Scaling ramps to 100% on failover.
explanations.backup_restore: Nothing provisioned in DR region.
explanations.active_active: Full-capacity clusters in each Region so either absorbs the other's load with no ramp; total compute roughly doubles.

explanations.backup_restore: Per-user subscription service, not region-bound infrastructure. Nothing runs in a DR region; the subscription follows the users.
explanations.pilot_light: Same as backup restore: no regional footprint to keep warm.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as backup restore: subscription pricing is unaffected by DR posture.
explanations.active_active: Same as backup restore: one subscription regardless of how many regions the workload spans.

explanations.backup_restore: Legacy Cost Explorer billing name for what is now Amazon Q Developer. Per-user subscription, not region-bound; nothing to replicate for DR.
explanations.pilot_light: Same as backup restore: no regional footprint to keep warm.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as backup restore: subscription pricing is unaffected by DR posture.
explanations.active_active: Same as backup restore: one subscription regardless of how many regions the workload spans.

explanations.backup_restore: Shield Advanced is one monthly subscription per consolidated-billing family covering all subscribed accounts and regions; protecting DR-region resources adds no second subscription.
explanations.pilot_light: Same subscription covers DR-region resources. Usage-based data-transfer-out fees track protected traffic, which is near zero in standby.
explanations.warm_standby: Same subscription covers DR-region resources; standby traffic keeps usage fees negligible.
explanations.active_active: One subscription still covers both regions. Usage-based fees follow traffic, which splits rather than doubles.

explanations.backup_restore: Serverless inference billed per token; no provisioned capacity to replicate. Prompts, agents, and knowledge-base configs are redeployable artifacts.
explanations.pilot_light: No invocations in the DR region means no charges; on-demand inference has nothing standing to keep warm.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light for on-demand inference. Note: Provisioned Throughput, if purchased in DR, would bill directly and is not covered by this multiplier.
explanations.active_active: Invocations split across regions; per-token billing means total inference cost is unchanged.

explanations.backup_restore: Resilience Hub is the DR assessment tooling itself, billed per application assessed; it is not workload infrastructure that gets a DR replica.
explanations.pilot_light: Same as backup restore: assessment tooling, not a DR target.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as backup restore: assessment tooling, not a DR target.
explanations.active_active: Same as backup restore: assessment tooling, not a DR target.

explanations.backup_restore: GuardDuty bills per region on analyzed volume: CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS query logs. Enabling it in the DR region (best practice regardless of DR posture) analyzes only the small event volume a mostly-empty region generates.
explanations.pilot_light: Same basis as backup restore: the DR region's analyzed volume is driven by its tiny footprint (replication endpoints, standby data services), a small fraction of the busy primary.
explanations.warm_standby: The warm fleet raises DR-region flow-log and DNS-log volume somewhat, but analyzed volume still trails the traffic-serving primary by a wide margin.
explanations.active_active: Analyzed traffic volume splits across regions rather than doubling; the residual increase is the per-region baseline of CloudTrail management activity now analyzed in two regions.

explanations.pilot_light: Key creation ($1/mo each) + reduced API usage (encrypt/decrypt). Traffic not active so API usage decreases slightly.
explanations.warm_standby: Same as pilot light: replica keys carry the per-key monthly fee regardless of posture, and API call volume tracks data replication activity, which does not change between standby postures.
explanations.backup_restore: Same as pilot light - keys needed for encrypted data at rest.
explanations.active_active: Keys and API usage double across both regions for all activities including read-only replication.

explanations.pilot_light: Neptune global database: a secondary cluster with reduced instance sizes replicates continuously. DR storage and replicated write I/Os mirror the primary; reduced compute keeps the total below 1x.
explanations.warm_standby: Same shape as pilot light: a reduced-size secondary cluster in the global database, ready to promote on failover.
explanations.backup_restore: Neptune cross-region snapshot copies are full copies each time (no incremental cross-region backups), so recurring data transfer plus DR-region backup storage add up to a substantial fraction of cluster spend.
explanations.active_active: Neptune has no native active-active; the secondary cluster in a global database is read-only. The posture is the same reduced-size secondary as warm standby, so the cost matches warm standby.

explanations.backup_restore: The VPC line is mostly hourly charges (interface endpoints, NAT gateways) plus usage-based data processing. Pre-deploying the network skeleton in DR duplicates a small slice of endpoint hours; with no traffic there is almost no data processing.

explanations.active_active: Both regions carry full networking surface: NAT gateway hours and data processing in the DR region approach the primary's as traffic splits and replication flows between regions.
